sections.h2: The one approved canopy case reached 5.1 metres, short of the 5.4 metre target

chart.title: Auchinleck's approved canopy stopped at 5.1 metres, below the industry's 5.4

sections.means: East Ayrshire Council approved the raise from 4.5 metres to 5.1 metres under planning policy.
sections.todo: Check any planned canopy height with the planning authority and a structural engineer before budgeting.

sections.h2: A double-deck trailer carries up to 52 pallets, double a single-deck's 26

chart.title: Double-decking doubles pallet capacity, not the 60% increase often quoted
chart.sub: UK-standard pallets carried per trailer of the same length.

sections.means: The 50% trunking-trip cut applies only to volume-constrained freight, not weight-constrained freight.
sections.todo: Use the corrected double-deck figures, not the 60% claim, when comparing trailer options.

sections.h2: Common vehicle heights of 4.2 and 4.95 metres sit below the 5.03 metre standard

chart.title: Flatbeds and double-deck trailers sit under the DMRB headroom benchmark
chart.sub: Commonly cited vehicle and structure heights, metres.
chart.source: DMRB CD 127; UK haulage industry guidance.

sections.means: Great Britain sets no legal maximum HGV height, so the 5.03 metre figure is a design benchmark, not a statute.
sections.todo: Treat the DMRB figures and the corrected double-deck numbers as the load-bearing facts when budgeting a canopy.
